title: A shortfall accrues penalties per second automatically, making the on-chain monitor an interim penalty ledger
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.3.1 specifies that where a Prime Agent's OVRC is less than its Aggregate RRC, "the shortfall will be logged and penalty accrual will commence on a pro-rata, per-second basis for the duration and magnitude of the observed shortfall, according to the penalty schedule defined in the Atlas. Thus, this on-chain monitoring system serves as an interim penalty ledger."

Three properties make this more than an alarm. Enforcement is **continuous** — there is no reporting boundary at which a shortfall becomes chargeable, so a Prime cannot be undercapitalised between snapshots for free. It is **proportional in two dimensions**, so a brief small gap and a sustained large one are priced differently rather than both counting as one violation. And it is **automatic**, requiring no discretionary finding before a liability exists.

The cost of automation is accepting known measurement error. Because the trigger is OVRC rather than TRC, the ledger charges against a figure the Atlas itself says can be wrong in both directions — hence "interim."

The design pattern is worth naming: accrue against the imperfect signal immediately, then correct against the authoritative record later. The alternative — waiting for verified data before any liability attaches — would leave enforcement silent during exactly the window when a shortfall is doing damage.
description: Where OVRC falls below Aggregate RRC, penalty accrual starts pro-rata on duration and magnitude without human involvement, producing a provisional liability that later reconciliation revises.
